info.description:
TORDLH

The National Weather Service in Duluth MN has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Southern Pine County in east central Minnesota...
Burnett County in northwestern Wisconsin...

* Until 545 PM CDT.

* At 511 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Branstad, or 13 miles southeast of Pine City,
moving northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Grantsburg and Branstad around 515 PM CDT.
Siren and Webster around 530 PM CDT.

Other locations in the path of this tornadic thunderstorm include
Saint Croix Band Pike Lake Area.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

This cluster of thunderstorms is capable of producing tornadoes and
widespread significant wind damage. Do not wait to see or hear the
tornado. For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest
floor of a building.

parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 5:30 PM CDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORMPX

The National Weather Service in the Twin Cities has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Southeastern Dakota County in east central Minnesota...
Northwestern Goodhue County in southeastern Minnesota...
Southwestern Pierce County in west central Wisconsin...

* Until 530 PM CDT.

* At 453 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Stanton, or 9 miles northeast of Northfield,
moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* This tornado will be near...
Cannon Falls around 500 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by the tornado include Randolph, Lake
Byllesby, Hampton, New Trier and Miesville.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Henry was last seen wearing a green shirt, green pants, and black shoes. Henry Moss was last observed on October 26, 2026, at approximately 1400 hours, on foot from the area of 59th Avenue and west Northern Avenue, Glendale, Arizona, Maricopa County. Henry is reported to have a medical condition that may cause confusion, raising concern for his safety and well-being.

info.headline: Sedgwick County testing outdoor warning devices
info.description: Sedgwick County Emergency Management will be testing the Outdoor Warning Sirens at Noon Today. Sedgwick County outdoor warning sirens are tested every Monday at Noon except Holidays and when threatening weather is present. Today we will be testing the Alert mode for one minute. The Alert Mode is a steady tone used for Tornado warning The Attack Mode is a classic rise and fall sound used for Air Attack Warning in times of war. Outdoor warning sirens are designed to be an early warning device primarily for persons who are outside away from the television and or radio. Remember when the outdoor warning sirens sound Take cover Tune in to local media Take action.
info.instruction: Emergency Management officials highly recommend citizens keep a NOAA weather radio in their homes preferably in the bedroom with a tone alert for those times when you are not monitoring public media. This broadcast originates from Sedgwick County Emergency Management located at seven fourteen North Main Wichita Kansas. WPMQ three ninety one. No action required test only.

AN AMBER ALERT IS BEING ISSUED BY THE CALIFORNIA HIGHWAY PATROL ON BEHALF OF THE WESTMINSTER DEPARTMENT.

ON OCTOBER 25, 2026, AT 400 PM, JOSEPH GARCIA WAS ABDUCTED FROM WESTMINSTER, CALIFORNIA.  JOSEPH GARCIA IS A 6 YEAR OLD HISPANIC MALE, 3 FEET 7 INCHES TALL, WEIGHING 65 POUNDS, WITH BROWN HAIR AND BROWN EYES.  JOSEPH IS BELIEVED TO BE WEARING A BEIGE SHIRT, BLUE SHORTS AND BLACK SHOES.

THE SUSPECT, FRANK RAMIREZ, IS A 47 YEAR OLD HISPANIC MALE, STANDING 5 FEET 7 INCHES TALL, WEIGHING 180 POUNDS WITH BLACK HAIR AND HAZEL EYES.   FRANK RAMIREZ IS BELIEVED TO BE WEARING A GRAY SLEEVELESS SHIRT AND SHORTS. 

THE SUSPECT WAS LAST SEEN DRIVING A 1995 BLUE GMC SONOMA, WITH CALIFORNIA LICENSE PLATE NUMBER 5 B 3 0 1 2 7.

IF SEEN CALL 9 1 1

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 11:15 PM MDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
TOREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northwestern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1115 PM MDT.

* At 1045 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 4 miles south of Desert Haven, moving east at
20 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northwestern Hudspeth County.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 25 at 7:09PM MDT until October 25 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR SOUTHWESTERN EDDY COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 709 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad Caverns National Park and Whites City.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
South Central Quay County in east central New Mexico...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 326 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 10 miles south of Ragland, or 30 miles northeast of
Fort Sumner, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Ragland, Mcalister and Forrest.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 7:30 PM MDT. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 7:30 PM MDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.description:
TORABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northeastern Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 730 PM MDT.

* At 701 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Santa Fe, moving north at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Santa Fe, Tesuque, Hyde Memorial State Park, Agua Fria and
Chupadero.

This includes Interstate 25 between Mile Markers 279 and 284.
info.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

Si esta al aire libre, en una casa movil, o en un vehiculo, debe ir al edificio seguro mas cercano y protegerse de proyectiles. Consulte los medios informativos.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...
East Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 653 PM MDT, Local law enforcement reported thunderstorms having
produced heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 3.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring. Interstate
40 between mile markers 102 and 108 has been closed due to
flooding.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Laguna Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, Acoma Pueblo, San Fidel, Cubero,
McCartys, New Laguna, Cebolletita and San Mateo.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 92 and 114.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 915 PM MDT.

* At 616 PM MDT, emergency management reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain in Magado Creek near Capitan. Flash flooding
is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lincoln, Capitan, Smokey Bear Historical Park, Lincoln State
Monument and Angus.

This includes Highway 380 between Mile Markers 79 and 98.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

South Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico... * Until 800 PM MDT. * At 504 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding in and around the South Fork Burn Scar. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the South Fork Burn Scar. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood. This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The South Fork burn scar in...
South Central Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 800 PM MDT.

* At 504 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Between 0.25 and 0.75
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2
inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
info.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...
East Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 451 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.75 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Laguna Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, Acoma Pueblo, San Fidel, Cubero,
McCartys, New Laguna, Cebolletita and San Mateo.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 92 and 114.
info.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:49PM MST until October 24 at 6:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 645 PM MST.

* At 349 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the Sycamore Creek drainage, around 10 miles east
of Cordes Junction. Between 1 and 2.25 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Dugas and Cedar Bench Wilderness.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Agua Fria River, Sycamore Creek, Little Ash Creek, Indian Creek,
Bishop Creek, Cold Water Creek, Chasm Creek, Silver Creek, South
Prong Sycamore Creek, Gap Creek, Dry Creek and Little Sycamore
Creek.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

info.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
TOREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 420 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 7 miles west of Pinon, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Weed around 430 PM MDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Avis,
Miller Flats, and McDonald Flats.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

info.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...
East Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 101 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Laguna Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, Acoma Pueblo, San Fidel, Cubero,
McCartys, New Laguna, Cebolletita and San Mateo.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 92 and 114.
info.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Find an
alternate route.

info.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
TOREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
East central Sierra County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 600 PM MDT.

* At 536 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Spaceport America, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and ping pong ball size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Cutter and Spaceport America around 540 PM MDT.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 4:15 PM MDT. Take shelter now. Check media.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 4:15 PM MDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

info.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
TOREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
East central Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...
North central Luna County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 346 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 5 miles southwest of Faywood, moving northeast at 30
mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and ping pong ball size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Faywood around 350 PM MDT.
Sherman around 400 PM MDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include
Gallinas Canyon and City Of Rocks State Park.
info.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 8:42PM MDT until October 22 at 11:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM

parameter.name: NWSheadline
parameter.value: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1130 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR SOUTHEASTERN CIBOLA COUNTY

parameter.name: CMAMtext
parameter.value: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.

parameter.name: CMAMlongtext
parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
At 842 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Acoma Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, San Fidel, Cubero, New Laguna,
Acomita, Acomita Lake, Seama, North Acomita Village and Paraje.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 99 and 112, as well
as Reservation Road 23.
info.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

parameter.value: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 12:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

info.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until midnight MST.

* At 732 PM MST, local law enforcement reported flooding across Lacy
Lane in Camp Verde. Flash flooding is continuing through Wet Beaver
Creek.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Montezuma, Montezuma Castle National Monument, Montezuma Well
and Lawrence Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Dry Beaver Creek, Rarick Canyon, Beaver Creek, Walker Creek and
Verde River.
info.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable.
